excerpt: Identify Sharjah apartment rental costs beyond annual rent, including deposits, attestation, utility setup, moving and lease obligations.
introduction:
The advertised rent is only one part of the money needed to rent an apartment in Sharjah. A tenant may need cash for a security deposit, brokerage, contract attestation, utility setup and moving. The amounts and responsibilities depend on the actual agreement and providers, so request an itemised written quote before paying.

The example below separates refundable deposits from expenses and uses sample numbers. Use the example to organise the upfront and recurring costs of the rental home you choose.
takeaways: Ask for the complete payment schedule and each extra charge in writing.
Deposits affect move-in cash even if they may be returned later.
Check attestation, utilities, maintenance and early-exit terms for the specific lease.

sections.heading: Which costs can sit outside the rent?
sections.body:
Ask the landlord or authorised agent for the annual rent, number and dates of payments, security deposit, brokerage and other charges. Confirm whether each amount is refundable, who receives it and what conditions apply. Add all rent instalments, deposits and lease charges to see the full tenancy cost.

Sharjah Municipality's [residential tenancy contract template](https://portal.shjmun.gov.ae/en/eservices/Attachements/Residential-Tenancy-Contract-Template.pdf) describes attestation and the parties' obligations under the referenced law. Confirm the current procedure, deadline and charges with the municipality for the agreement; do not rely on a fee quoted for another emirate or an old contract.

The [Al Majaz and Al Taawun family rental guide](/journal/al-majaz-vs-al-taawun-family-rental-comparison) provides location context, but the actual lease determines the terms.

sections.heading: Calculate example move-in cash
sections.body:
Suppose a sample lease has AED 45,000 annual rent in four equal payments, so the first payment is AED 11,250. Add an assumed AED 2,500 security deposit, AED 2,250 brokerage, AED 1,000 contract-related charge, AED 1,500 utility deposit and AED 1,500 moving cost. The initial cash requirement is AED 20,000.

These example amounts show how move-in payments and refundable deposits fit together. The chart separates the components. Security and utility deposits may be refundable under their terms, but the cash is still needed at move-in.

The other three rent instalments total AED 33,750. Put them on a calendar and budget for actual utility consumption, internet, furniture and other costs separately.

chart.note: Sample inputs total AED 20,000; actual fees and deposit return terms vary.

sections.heading: Clarify utilities and cooling
sections.body:
Ask whether electricity, water and cooling are included in rent, separately metered or billed under another arrangement. Confirm the provider, account setup, deposit and any fixed charges for the apartment. The [Sharjah Electricity, Water and Gas Authority move-in service](https://eservice.sewa.gov.ae/Portal/PreStartService.aspx) includes tenancy information and document fields for a new account. Verify the current process and amount directly.

Ask whether the previous account has been settled and when services will be available. For a separate cooling provider, request the billing basis and any fixed and consumption charges. Check internet installation and contract length as well.

Recent bills, if available, can provide context but do not guarantee your household's future consumption.

sections.heading: Read maintenance and deposit terms
sections.body:
Check who arranges and pays for routine repairs, major equipment faults, pest control and damage. Ask how to report a problem and what is included in the apartment. Inspect cooling, plumbing, locks, appliances and visible marks before handover.

Agree a dated condition record and inventory with the landlord, including photographs where appropriate. Ask how deposit deductions are assessed and when any balance will be returned. A furnished apartment should have a list of items and their condition.

Read notice, renewal and early-termination clauses. Seek written clarification or qualified advice if the agreement is unclear; a verbal assurance should not be assumed to override a different written term.

sections.heading: Plan costs that arise later
sections.body:
Ask whether renewal has an attestation or administration charge and check the notice dates. Put rent cheques, school payments and insurance renewals on a calendar alongside income. A monthly average can hide several large payments due at the same time.

Check the building's move-in rules, lift booking and parking. If a refundable building deposit is required, record the cash requirement and the return conditions separately. Obtain current amounts for the particular tower rather than assuming a standard fee.

Keep a reserve for unexpected household costs and review the budget when a lease, commute or school arrangement changes.

sections.heading: Compare complete annual costs
sections.body:
Use one worksheet per home: annual rent, known non-refundable fees, expected utilities, transport, parking and any necessary furniture. Show deposits separately. A higher advertised rent with some services included can be less expensive than a lower rent with separate bills.

Inspect the actual apartment and verify the landlord's authority before transferring a deposit. Request a written quote and keep the agreement, receipts and contact details. The [Sharjah family area guide](/journal/best-areas-to-buy-property-in-sharjah-for-families) offers context for a wider search.

sections.heading: Questions to settle before a deposit
sections.body:
Verify that the person offering the unit is authorised to lease it and that the payment instructions belong to the correct party. Ask whether the deposit reserves the exact apartment, how long the reservation lasts and what happens if the lease is not completed. Obtain those terms and a receipt in writing.

Confirm the apartment number, parking, included appliances and move-in date in the agreement. If a repair or cleaning is promised, record who will complete it and by when. These checks help prevent an apparently small upfront payment from becoming an unexpected cost or dispute.

sections.heading: Ask for current rental options
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Sharjah project collection](/projects?emirate=Sharjah) for local context and ask which relevant rental homes are currently available. [Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget and preferred area.

Request the exact apartment, payment dates and itemised lease costs, then confirm current official and utility requirements before signing.
